message.content:
Yes—Atlanta residents can file a noise complaint with the city’s local authorities. Here’s how you can do it: | Step | What to Do | Where to Go / Who to Call | |------|------------|---------------------------| | **1** | **Check the city’s noise ordinance** – Atlanta’s “Noise Ordinance” (Title 10, Chapter 2 of the Atlanta Municipal Code) sets the rules and times for acceptable noise levels. You can read it online at the City of Atlanta’s official website. | | **2** | **File a complaint online** – Use the City of Atlanta’s “Report a Problem” portal. Search for “noise complaint” or “code enforcement” and fill out the form.
URL: https://www.atlantaga.gov/311 | | **3** | **Call the Atlanta Police Department (APD)** – For urgent or ongoing noise issues, you can call the APD’s non‑emergency line at **404‑656‑4000** or dial **311** from within Atlanta. | | **4** | **Visit City Hall** – If you prefer in‑person, go to the City Hall (200 Peachtree Street NE, Atlanta, GA 30303) and speak with the Code Enforcement or Public Safety office. | | **5** | **Follow up** – After filing, you’ll receive a reference number. Keep it handy for any follow‑up questions or status checks. | **Quick Tips** - **Time limits:** Noise complaints are most effective when filed during the hours the ordinance specifies (usually 10 p.m.–7 a.m. on weekdays and 11 p.m.–7 a.m. on weekends). - **Documentation:** If possible, note the time, location, and nature of the noise. Audio recordings or photos can help the authorities assess the situation. - **Repeat offenses:** If the same source repeatedly violates the ordinance, the city may issue a citation or take further enforcement action. So, yes—you can report a noise complaint to your local council (the City of Atlanta) through the methods above.
